```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import os
os.chdir(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), ".."))   # analysis/logistic_laplace_simulations -> analysis
os.chdir("..")                                # -> twogroup_experiments/
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "analysis/logistic_laplace_simulations")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.rcParams["figure.dpi"] = 110
import polars as pl
import cs_tables as C
import delta_figure as F
import posterior_figure as PF
import laplacelib as R

SC_G, SC_N = "023-laplace-gaussian", "024-laplace-nested"
dg = C.declared(C.load(SC_G)); sg = dg.filter(~pl.col("null"))
dn = C.declared(C.load(SC_N)); sn = dn.filter(~pl.col("null"))
```

Two analogs of the [022 full grid](full_grid.qmd). The protocol is 022's: $p = 256$,
$b_0 = -2$, $L^* = 3$ equal causals at gap 8 (correlated) or 64 (independent), fit with
$L = 5$, EB prior variance, the same five arms in $\mathcal{Q}_2$, 200 replicates per cell.
Only the design and its sweep change.

- **023, Gaussian.** AR(1) Gaussian columns, $n = 500$, adjacent $\rho = 0.9$ (causal-causal
  latent correlation $0.9^8 = 0.43$ at gap 8, $\approx 0$ at gap 64). Every column is dense and
  $N(0, 1)$, so there is no set-size axis; the sweep is the signal $T = E[\text{LRT}]$ per
  causal in $\{4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24\}$, with one $\beta$ per $T$. The dense control for 022's
  sparse-set findings.
- **024, nested.** `binary_attrition_X`: Markov roots (phi 0.8, half the rows) expanded into 32
  blocks of 8 nested sets, each step keeping 55% of the parent's members, so one matrix holds
  sets from 500 members down to 8. $n = 1000$. The sweep is the causals' depth $d \in 0..7$,
  i.e. their expected size $500 \cdot 0.55^d$ (022's $m$), with $\beta$ per $(d, T)$ and
  $T \in \{8, 16\}$. Causals sit at the same depth in blocks gap/8 apart; their decoys are
  their own ancestors and descendants at other sizes.

All CS metrics are over **declared** CSs (component $\log \text{BF} \ge 2$), as in 022.

```{python}
#| label: status
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
for sc, d, s, keys in ((SC_G, dg, sg, ["T", "gap"]), (SC_N, dn, sn, ["T", "gap", "depth"])):
    reps = s.group_by(keys + ["method"]).len()["len"]
    print(f"- `{sc}`: {s.select(keys).unique().height} signal cells x {s['method'].n_unique()} arms, "
          f"{reps.min()}-{reps.max()} reps per cell; {d.filter(pl.col('null')).height // max(d.filter(pl.col('null'))['method'].n_unique(), 1)} null reps per arm.")
```

# 023: Gaussian design, signal axis {#sec-gauss}

## Headline: per gap, pooled over T {#sec-gauss-pooled}

```{python}
#| label: tab-gauss-pooled
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print("CAVI-Q2 in absolute terms; every other arm as **arm minus CAVI-Q2** on the same "
      "replicates. *coverage*: fraction of declared CSs containing a causal. *size*: median "
      "declared-CS size with its interquartile range. *power*: mean over reps of the fraction "
      "of the 3 causals captured by a declared CS. *CS/fit*: declared CSs per fit. 95% CIs "
      "resample replicates, jointly for both arms of a difference. One row per T x gap cell "
      "(there is no size axis to pool over).\n")
print(C.pooled_summary(dg, ref="cavi"))
```

## Along T {#sec-gauss-along}

```{python}
#| label: fig-gauss-delta
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Credible set metrics, relative to CAVI, Gaussian design. AR(1) Gaussian columns ($n = 500$, $p = 256$, $\\rho = 0.9$), $L^* = 3$, fit $L = 5$, 200 replicates per cell. The x axis is the signal per causal, $T = E[\\mathrm{LRT}]$ against the null; every column is $N(0, 1)$ so $\\beta$ is one number per $T$. Columns: correlated (gap 8, latent $r = 0.43$) or independent (gap 64) causals. Rows: coverage of declared 95% credible sets, power, and mean credible set size as a ratio (log axis), each as the arm minus CAVI-Q2 on the same replicates; dashed line: no difference. Bands: 95% intervals from resampling replicates."
F.draw(F.delta_frame(dg, ref="cavi", axis="T", panels=("gap",)), ref="cavi");
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-gauss-absolute
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Credible set metrics, absolute, Gaussian design. Same layout; each arm's own coverage (dashed: nominal 0.95), power, and mean credible set size (log axis), with per-arm 95% intervals from resampling replicates."
F.draw(F.delta_frame(dg, ref=None, axis="T", panels=("gap",)), ref=None);
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-gauss-pip
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-gauss-effect
```

## Along depth {#sec-nested-along}

The x axis is the causal sets' expected density $\theta = 0.5 \cdot 0.55^d$, i.e. their
expected size over $n = 1000$, so it reads like 022's density axis: 0.5 is the root (500
members), 0.008 is depth 7 (8 members).

```{python}
#| label: fig-nested-delta
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Credible set metrics, relative to CAVI, nested design. Attrition blocks ($n = 1000$, $p = 256$, roots at density 0.5 shrinking 0.55x per step over 8 depths), $L^* = 3$ causals at one depth, fit $L = 5$, 200 replicates per cell. The x axis is the causals' expected density $0.5 \\cdot 0.55^d$ for depth $d = 0..7$; $\\beta$ is calibrated per depth so $E[\\mathrm{LRT}] = T$. Columns: signal ($T = 8, 16$) over causal correlation (gap 8: same depth in adjacent blocks; gap 64: 8 blocks apart). Rows and bands as in the Gaussian figure."
F.draw(F.delta_frame(dn, ref="cavi"), ref="cavi");
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-nested-absolute
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Credible set metrics, absolute, nested design. Each arm's own coverage (dashed: nominal 0.95), power, and mean credible set size (log axis), with per-arm 95% intervals from resampling replicates."
F.draw(F.delta_frame(dn, ref=None), ref=None);
```
